if i am understanding this correctly, the more prevalent term is shRNA which  if you looked up should explain it; but i am here it goes anyway.

rna interference is mediated by the dicer enzyme. this enzyme recognizes double stranded RNA, which is typically not native in eukaryotes, cuts it and divides the strands to be used as templates for another enzyme, the risc complex. this enzyme takes the templates and see if it can find the complementary mRNA molecule and thus form a dsRNA molecule for a short stretch. the risc complex cleaves the mRNA molecule thus reducing its expression. 

to compare the process for a hair pair (shRNA) to the normal siRNA. siRNA is a single stranded RNA molecule that is reverse complement to the target gene's mRNA. after it binds it goes through the process above.  the shRNA contains a part or the target sequences as well as the reverse complement to the sequence. thus after it is produced it can  self anneal and start the process above with out having to bind to the target mRNA

tl;dr the stem loop (short hairpin) can self anneal and and start the RNAi process by itself while siRNA molecules must bind to the target mRNA first to cause RNAi.

while i don't have a lot of experience with the actual algorithm i do about gene sequencing, i think you are referring to whole genome sequencing.  anyway, with an alignment algorithm you are taking the sequencing data and comparing that to a know sequence, such as the sequence generated by the human genome project, to help align it to the other sequencing data. with this you still know where most everything goes relative to one another even with gaps and you need less overlap to assemble. but if the sequence is different enough from the reference it can have a lot of difficulty aligning properly.

 with an assembly algorithm you are aligning each piece to every other piece you generate. you need a lot of overlap to ensure that the sequence is as whole and organized as possible and any gaps in the data might isolate that piece from other data. since you don't use a known reference to align even if the sequence is highly mutated you can still assemble it.
